tests.name: Law Admission Test
tests.short: The national entry test for the five-year LLB programme.
tests.audience: Intermediate (HSSC) students who want to study law
tests.purpose: To make sure that only students with the basic reasoning, language and general knowledge needed for legal study enter law programmes. Following the Supreme Court’s decision on legal education reforms, LAT is mandatory for admission to LLB programmes in all public and private universities and law colleges in Pakistan.
tests.eligibility: Students who have completed, or are completing, intermediate (HSSC) or equivalent and wish to study law.
tests.measures: Reading and comprehension in English, logical and analytical reasoning, general knowledge and written expression, as announced in the official test pattern.
tests.frequencyNote: Bi-annual, as directed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan (Para 15(2)).
tests.resultsUse: Universities use the LAT result as a required eligibility condition in their LLB admission process.
tests.patternNote: Section weightings, number of questions and timing are published in the official LAT test pattern for each session.
tests.reliability: KR-20 / alpha for each section and total; parallel forms for the two annual sessions; rubric-based marking for any written component.

sections.name: Logical & analytical reasoning
sections.detail: Drawing valid conclusions and spotting patterns in arguments.

sections.name: General knowledge
sections.detail: Awareness of national and international affairs.

sections.name: Written expression
sections.detail: Communicating ideas clearly and correctly in writing.

tests.name: Law Graduate Assessment Test
tests.short: The licensing-type test for law graduates seeking enrolment as Advocates.
tests.audience: LLB graduates seeking enrolment with a provincial Bar Council
tests.purpose: To confirm that law graduates meet a minimum standard of legal knowledge before entering practice. LAW-GAT is mandatory for law graduates who wish to enrol as Advocates in any Bar Council.
tests.eligibility: Holders of an LLB degree seeking enrolment with a provincial Bar Council.
tests.measures: Knowledge and application of core areas of law, drawn from a question bank prepared specially for the test.
tests.frequencyNote: Held across Pakistan every quarter, as directed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan (Para 15(1)).
tests.resultsUse: A pass result is required for enrolment as an Advocate. Because it is a pass/fail decision, ETC pays special attention to accuracy around the passing score.
tests.patternNote: The pass mark is set through a documented standard-setting process, and scores are equated across quarterly sessions so the standard stays the same.
tests.reliability: Total-score reliability; decision consistency and SEM at the passing score; equating across quarterly sessions.

sections.name: Core areas of law
sections.detail: Knowledge and application of the core legal subjects expected of a new advocate.

sections.name: Legal reasoning & application
sections.detail: Applying legal principles to practical situations.

tests.name: Higher Education Aptitude Test
tests.short: The gateway test for MS/MPhil study and HEC scholarships.
tests.purpose: Eligibility for HEC scholarship awards and for MS/MPhil admissions in public and private universities. HAT-General is offered in five categories, grouped by broad field of study, so that candidates are assessed in a context close to their own discipline.
tests.eligibility: Graduates holding a 16-year degree (or equivalent) who wish to pursue MS/MPhil study.
tests.measures: General academic aptitude: verbal reasoning, quantitative reasoning and analytical reasoning.
tests.frequencyNote: Session dates are published in official ETC notices.
tests.resultsUse: Universities and HEC use HAT scores to confirm eligibility and to rank candidates for admission or scholarships.
tests.patternNote: Offered in 5 categories grouped by broad field of study. Category list and section weightings are published with each session’s announcement.
tests.reliability: KR-20 / alpha by section (verbal, quantitative, analytical) and total; comparability across the five categories and sessions.

sections.name: Verbal reasoning
sections.detail: Vocabulary, sentence completion, analogies and comprehension.

sections.name: Quantitative reasoning
sections.detail: Arithmetic, algebra, geometry and data interpretation.

tests.name: Higher Education Aptitude & Achievement Test
tests.short: Aptitude plus subject achievement for PhD admissions and scholarships.
tests.audience: MS/MPhil (18-year) degree holders applying for PhD programmes
tests.purpose: Eligibility for HEC scholarship awards and for PhD admissions in public and private universities. HAAT-Subject combines general aptitude with subject-specific achievement, so it shows both how well a candidate reasons and how deeply they know their own field.
tests.eligibility: Holders of an MS/MPhil (or equivalent 18-year) degree applying for PhD programmes.
tests.measures: Advanced reasoning skills plus in-depth knowledge of the candidate’s subject, reviewed by subject committees.
tests.frequencyNote: Session dates and subject lists are published in official ETC notices.
tests.resultsUse: Universities and HEC use the result as an eligibility condition and for merit ranking of PhD candidates.
tests.patternNote: Subject papers are developed and reviewed by subject committees.
tests.reliability: Reliability by subject paper; item-bank calibration for each subject; equivalence of subject forms.

sections.name: Aptitude
sections.detail: Advanced verbal, quantitative and analytical reasoning.

sections.name: Subject achievement
sections.detail: In-depth knowledge of the candidate’s own discipline.

tests.name: Undergraduate Studies Admission Test
tests.short: Undergraduate admissions and HEC undergraduate scholarships, in six streams.
tests.purpose: A standardized test for admission to undergraduate programmes and for HEC undergraduate scholarships. USAT is offered in six categories matched to the candidate’s intermediate stream, and every version has the same two-part structure.
tests.eligibility: Students who have completed, or are completing, intermediate (HSSC), A-level or equivalent.
tests.measures: Foundational concepts in the chosen discipline, general cognitive aptitude (verbal and quantitative reasoning), applied problem-solving, and written construction and justification.
tests.frequencyNote: Session dates are published in official ETC notices.
tests.resultsUse: Universities and HEC use USAT results for undergraduate admission and scholarship decisions.
tests.patternNote: Part I is machine-scored; Part II essays are marked against predefined rubrics by trained examiners, with a sample double-marked.
tests.reliability: KR-20 / alpha for Part I (75 MCQs) and each section; inter-rater agreement for Part II essays (double-marking of a sample).
syllabus: Verbal reasoning (analogy, synonym/antonym, sentence completion, comprehension)
Quantitative reasoning (arithmetic, algebra, geometry, equations, statistics, mental maths)

sections.name: Part I — Common Core
sections.detail: 20 Verbal Reasoning + 25 Quantitative Reasoning MCQs, taken by everyone.

sections.name: Part I — Discipline-specific
sections.detail: 30 MCQs in the subjects of the candidate’s stream.

sections.name: Part II — Argument-based essay
sections.detail: One essay chosen from three options.

sections.name: Part II — Narrative essay
sections.detail: One essay chosen from three options.

tests.name: Customized Tests
tests.short: Tests built to order for recruitment, admission, screening and assessment.
tests.audience: Government departments, regulators, universities and projects
tests.purpose: ETC builds tests to order: recruitment tests for specific cadres, admission tests for individual universities (for example the Quaid-i-Azam University undergraduate admission test and MDCAT for SZABMU), scholarship tests, psychometric and personality evaluations, skill assessments and screening tests.
tests.eligibility: As defined by the client institution for each assessment.
tests.measures: Whatever the client’s decision requires: job-related knowledge, aptitude, skills, physical standards or personality traits.
tests.resultsUse: Results are processed, checked and delivered to the client with a result report and, where useful, analysis by learning outcome.
tests.patternNote: Every customized test follows the same blueprint, review, piloting and analysis process as the national products. ETC has developed 850 blueprints for distinct cadres to date.
tests.reliability: Reliability calculated for every administration; inter-rater checks for skill, descriptive and interview components.
syllabus: Defined with the client in the requirement study and blueprint

sections.name: MCQ-based tests
sections.detail: Objective questions, machine-scored quickly and without bias.

sections.name: Descriptive tests
sections.detail: Written answers scored against a fixed rubric by trained examiners.

sections.name: Skill & physical tests
sections.detail: Practical or measured tasks against defined standards.

sections.name: Psychological assessment
sections.detail: Standardized tools for personality, aptitude or behaviour.

notices.title: USAT December 2026 session: registration open
notices.summary: Online registration is open for all six USAT categories for the December 2026 session.
notices.bodyHtml:
Registration for the Undergraduate Studies Admission Test (USAT) December 2026 session is now open for USAT-E, USAT-M, USAT-CS, USAT-GS, USAT-COM and USAT-A.

Candidates must register and pay through the official ETC portal only. Admit cards will be available on the portal ten days before the test.

Please read the USAT syllabus and candidate instructions before registering.

notices.title: LAW-GAT Q4 2026: test schedule and centres announced
notices.summary: The fourth-quarter LAW-GAT will be held at ETC test centres across Pakistan. Registration closes soon.
notices.bodyHtml:
The Law Graduate Assessment Test (LAW-GAT) for the fourth quarter of 2026 will be held across Pakistan.

Test cities and centres will appear on admit cards. Candidates should arrive 60 minutes before the reporting time with their original CNIC and admit card.

notices.title: HAT-General November 2026: registration open
notices.summary: Registration is open for HAT-General in all five categories for MS/MPhil admission and HEC scholarships.
notices.bodyHtml:
Registration is open for the Higher Education Aptitude Test (HAT-General) November 2026 session.

Candidates should choose the category closest to their field of study. Category details are given in the attached notice.

notices.title: USAT September 2026 results announced
notices.summary: Results for the USAT September 2026 session are now available on the official results portal.
notices.bodyHtml:
Results for the USAT September 2026 session have been announced after post-hoc analysis of every item.

Candidates can view and download their result cards from the official ETC results portal using their roll number and CNIC.

notices.title: LAW-GAT Q3 2026 results announced
notices.summary: Pass/fail results for the third-quarter LAW-GAT are available on the official results portal.
notices.bodyHtml:
Results for LAW-GAT Q3 2026 have been announced. Successful candidates may proceed with enrolment at their provincial Bar Council.

Requests for result verification must be submitted within the period stated in the attached notice.

notices.title: LAT second session 2026: registration schedule
notices.summary: The Law Admission Test second session for 2026 is open for registration for LLB admissions.
notices.bodyHtml:
Registration for the second Law Admission Test (LAT) session of 2026 is open.

LAT is mandatory for admission to the five-year LLB programme at all public and private universities and law colleges in Pakistan.

notices.title: HAAT-Subject 2026: list of subject papers
notices.summary: The list of subject papers offered in the next HAAT-Subject session has been published.
notices.bodyHtml:
ETC has published the subject papers available in the next HAAT-Subject session for PhD admissions and HEC scholarships.

Candidates should confirm that their subject is listed before registering.

notices.title: Recruitment test for Federal Directorate of Education posts
notices.summary: ETC is conducting a recruitment test on behalf of the Federal Directorate of Education.
notices.bodyHtml:
ETC is conducting a recruitment test for advertised posts on behalf of the Federal Directorate of Education.

Shortlisted candidates will be informed through the official portal and SMS.

notices.title: USAT December 2026: test cities and centres
notices.summary: ETC will conduct the USAT December 2026 session in 40 cities across Pakistan.
notices.bodyHtml:
The USAT December 2026 session will be held at ETC test centres in 40 cities.

Candidates select their preferred test city during registration. Allocation is subject to seat availability.

notices.title: LAT first session 2026 results announced
notices.summary: Results for the first LAT session of 2026 are available on the official results portal.
notices.bodyHtml:
Results for the first Law Admission Test session of 2026 have been announced.

Universities and law colleges will use the LAT result as an eligibility condition in their LLB admission process.

notices.title: Special arrangements for candidates with disabilities
notices.summary: How to request reasonable arrangements for disabilities or special needs on test day.
notices.bodyHtml:
ETC provides reasonable arrangements for candidates with disabilities or special needs, on request.

Requests should be made during registration with supporting documents, so arrangements can be confirmed before the test.

notices.title: Reminder: unfair means and impersonation policy
notices.summary: Any form of cheating or impersonation leads to disciplinary action after a fair hearing.
notices.bodyHtml:
Candidates must do their own work honestly and keep test content confidential.

Cases of alleged unfair means are heard by the Quality Assurance Department through a documented procedure, and the candidate is always heard before a decision.

faqs.question: How do I register for an ETC test?
faqs.answer: Registration and fee payment are done only through the official ETC online portal. Read the official notice for your test, create an account on the portal, complete the form and pay the fee before the deadline.

faqs.question: Can I register for more than one test or category?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the test schedules do not clash. Each registration is separate and needs its own fee. For USAT and HAT-General, choose the category that matches your stream or field of study.

faqs.question: I made a mistake in my registration form. Can I correct it?
faqs.answer: Corrections are allowed through the portal until the registration deadline. After the deadline, contact the ETC helpline with your registration details.

faqs.question: Which identity document do I need?
faqs.answer: Use your CNIC or B-Form (for under-18 candidates) when registering, and bring the original to the test centre.

faqs.question: When can I download my admit card (roll number slip)?
faqs.answer: Admit cards are usually available on the official portal about ten days before the test. The admit card shows your test centre, date and reporting time.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the test centre?
faqs.answer: Bring your admit card, original CNIC or B-Form, and only the items permitted in the candidate instructions. Mobile phones, smart watches and other electronic devices are not allowed.

faqs.question: What happens if I arrive late?
faqs.answer: Arrive by the reporting time printed on your admit card. Candidates who arrive after the gates close may not be allowed to sit the test, so the same rules apply to every candidate.

faqs.question: How is my identity checked at the centre?
faqs.answer: Staff verify you against your admit card and identity document at entry. This protects every candidate from impersonation.

faqs.question: When will results be announced?
faqs.answer: Results are announced after post-hoc analysis of every item and the whole test. The date is stated in the official notice, and results are published on the official results portal.

faqs.question: How is my test scored?
faqs.answer: MCQ answer sheets are scanned by OMR and scored automatically against a verified key. Any faulty item found in post-hoc analysis is removed from scoring or credited to all candidates. Essays are marked against a fixed rubric by trained examiners.

faqs.question: Can I request a re-check of my result?
faqs.answer: Yes. Requests for result verification can be made within the period stated in the result notification, through the official portal.

faqs.question: How long is my result valid?
faqs.answer: Validity depends on the test and on the institution using the result. Check the official notice for your test and the admission criteria of the university or programme.

faqs.question: How much does each test cost?
faqs.answer: As per the ETC Institutional Profile 2026: LAT Rs. 2,000; LAW-GAT Rs. 3,000; HAT-General Rs. 2,000; HAAT-Subject Rs. 3,000; USAT Rs. 2,000. Always confirm the current fee in the official announcement for each test.

faqs.question: Is the test fee refundable?
faqs.answer: Fee refund rules are stated in the official notice for each test. In general, fees are not refundable once registration closes.

faqs.question: Can I get special arrangements on test day?
faqs.answer: Yes. ETC provides reasonable arrangements for candidates with disabilities or special needs, on request. Apply during registration with supporting documents so arrangements can be confirmed before the test.

faqs.question: Is the test centre accessible for wheelchair users?
faqs.answer: Tell ETC about your needs when you register. ETC will allocate a suitable centre and seating wherever possible.

faqs.question: Can ETC design a test for our organization?
faqs.answer: Yes. ETC develops customized tests for recruitment, admission, psychometric evaluation, skill assessment and screening. Start with an institutional enquiry and ETC will arrange a requirement study.

faqs.question: How long does a customized test take to set up?
faqs.answer: It depends on the posts or programme, the number of candidates and whether new items must be written. The timeline is agreed with the client during the requirement study.

faqs.question: What does our institution receive after the test?
faqs.answer: Results are processed, checked and delivered with a result report and, where useful, analysis by learning outcome.
